questions.question: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon measures 9°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any regular polygon, the **sum of all exterior angles** is always 360°.

Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ Measure of each exterior angle

⇒ n = 360° ÷ 9°

⇒ n = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Measure of each **exterior angle** = 9°

**Formula Used:**

In a **regular polygon** with **n** sides, each exterior angle is given by: 360° / n

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89b172afbac57d32bcf93c8df7465f5a2f2a45a7e1af56edac38524e2805c04e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Each exterior angle = 360° / n

⇒ 9° = 360° / n

⇒ n = 360° / 9°

⇒ n = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of a polygon with n sides is (n − 2) × 180°.

Each Interior Angle

For a regular polygon, each interior angle is [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n or simply (180° − exterior angle).

Interior and Exterior Angle Relationship

At any vertex of a polygon, the sum of the interior angle and the exterior angle is always 180° (linear pair).</p

questions.question: A water tank has two holes. The 1st hole alone empties the tank in 9 minutes and 2ⁿd hole alone empties the tank in 6 minutes. If water leaks out at a constant rate, how many minutes does it take if both the holes together empty the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

1st hole empties the tank in 9 minutes and 2nd hole empties the tank in 6 minutes

Water leaks out at a constant rate

**Formula used:**

If a hole empties a tank in 'a' hours and an another empties the same tank in 'b' hours and if water leaks at a constant rate, then

Total work = LCM of the times taken by two holes = LCM of (a, b)

Efficiency of first hole = LCM of (a, b)/a

Efficiency of second hole = LCM of (a, b)/b

Combined efficiency of them = efficiency of 1st hole + efficiency of 2nd hole

Time taken to fill the tank = Total work/The combined efficiency of the holes 

**For alternate method,**

If a hole empties a tank in 'a' hours and an another empties the same tank in 'b' hours and if water leaks at a constant rate, the net part filled in 1 hour = 1/a + 1/b 

∴ Time taken to empty the tank = ab/(a + b) hours

**Calculation:**

Let the total work done to empty the tank be LCM of 9 and 6 i.e. 18 unit

Tank emptied by 1st hole in 1 minute = 18/9 = 2 unit

Tank emptied by 2nd hole in 1 minute = 18/6 = 3 unit

**∴ To completely empty the tank, Time taken together = 18/5 = **3(3)/(5)**minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f72be33799c08d3322a2907949d25e7543e352bc7880a277f6efed7f62d7c04b.png] 

1st hole empties the tank = 9 minutes

2nd hole empties the tank = 6 minutes

**Time taken to empty the tank = (9 × 6)/(9 + 6) = 54/15 = 18/5 = 3(3)/(5) minutes**

questions.question: How much time does a Geostationary satellite take to complete one orbit, at the height of 35790 km?
questions.solution:
__Concept__:

__
 
• Geostationary satellite: It is an earth-orbiting satellite placed at a height of about 36000 km from the earth's surface. A few characteristics of this satellite includes

 
 
• It revolves in an orbit that is aligned with the equatorial plane of the earth.
 
• It has the same direction of rotation as that of the earth i.e. from west to east.
 
• It rotates with the same angular speed as the earth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2afe5ff5962086292a70e1a95b2a45b85e775b34421a920962925c89d5d4cf14.png] 

 
• The time period of the satellite: It is the time taken by the satellite to complete one revolution around the Earth.

 
 
• Consider a satellite orbiting the earth at a height h from the surface of the earth of radius R.
 
• 
 
The circumference of orbit of satellite = 2π(R+h)

 
 
 
 
• 
 
The orbital velocity of the satellite at a height h is given by,

 

​⇒ v₀ =sqrt{(GM)/(R+h)}

Where M is the mass of the Earth.

The time period of the satellite is given by:

⇒ T = (circumference)/(orbital \: velocity) = (2pi(R+h))/(sqrt{frac{GM){R+h}}} = 2pisqrt{((R+h)³)/(GM)}

 

Explanation__:

__
 
• A satellite whose time period is 24 hours____ __and is revolving in an orbit concentric and coplanar with the equatorial plane of earth is called a geostationary satellite.

questions.question: Two bus start from a house at an interval of 10 minutes and travel at a speed of 20 km/hr. With how much speed (km/hr). should a man coming from the opposite direction towards the house travel, to meet the buses at an interval of 8 minutes?

**Given:**

**A _____________M_______________B**

**Calculation:**

Let Speed of the man is x kmph.
Distance covered in 10 minutes at 20 kmph = distance covered in 8 minutes at (20 + x) kmph.

Here relative speed = (20 + x) km/hour

⇒ 20 × 10/60 = 8/60 × (20 + x)
⇒ 200 = 160 + 8x
⇒ 8x = 40
∴ x = 5 kmph = speed of man

So at relative speed, (v + 20)km/hr, distance travelled in 8 min = 200/60 km

Applying distance = speed × time

200/60= (v + 20) × 8/60

v = 5km/hr
